title: *Visions from San Francisco Bay* - Marginal REVOLUTION
gist: Tyler Cowen quotes Czeslaw Milosz arguing that American capitalism's prodigality with private capital built a vast university-research-laboratory sector, while European capitalism's miserliness prevented laying its foundations, leaving a widening and possibly permanent gap.

insights.claim: Milosz characterizes American capitalism as founded on daring, resourcefulness, largesse, and waste, versus European capitalism founded on the single passion of miserliness.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: A cultural-capital lens on why the US and Europe diverge in risk appetite and investment, still cited in stagnation debates.
insights.quote: European capitalism was founded on one powerful passion — miserliness.
insights.locator: American capitalism was founded on daring

insights.claim: Milosz credits the prodigality of American private capital, later joined by tax money, with creating a vast new economic sector of universities, research institutes, and laboratories that Western Europe failed to produce.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Locates US research dominance in an early willingness to spend private capital that Europe's thrift foreclosed.
insights.quote: The prodigality of private capital in America made the beginnings possible; money from taxes joined in at the next stage.
insights.locator: American capitalism was founded on daring

insights.claim: Milosz argues European miserliness prevented laying the foundations for the research sector and doubts government treasuries will ever overcome the ever-widening gap with America.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: A pessimistic long-run view on Europe closing the research-and-innovation gap with the US.
insights.quote: it is doubtful whether the government treasuries will ever be able to over come ever-widening gap
